propositions: The inbound link differ is ADD-only by construction and never removes local deps when the corresponding Jira link is deleted, while the outbound direction has a removal path, creating asymmetry.
The apply layer silently drops any non-add link records via early exit at `action != 'add': continue`, so even if the differ emitted removals they would be discarded before reaching `rebar.unlink`.
A link deleted on the peer is re-added locally on the next pass due to the outbound ADD emitted when the local dep exists but the peer lacks it, causing churn rather than convergence.

Distinguishing a peer deletion from a never-pushed local link is impossible with only the current-pass state (both yield identical inputs: managed=true, peer_link_absent=true), requiring persisted peer-state history to arbitrate safely.

The ecosystem baseline treats link-deletion propagation as an opt-in advanced feature (Exalate), explicitly declines it citing data-loss risk (Aha), or leaves far-side items in place (Asana, Workfront), indicating this is not a parity gap.
